problem.text:
A crate of mass m rests on a level floor, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is mu. Starting from rest, the crate is pulled by a constant horizontal force F for a time t1. While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

v = 318 cm/s (the speed of the crate when the pull stops). m = 169 kg (the mass of the crate). Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Determine p, the momentum of the crate when the pull stops. Express the result in N s. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.
problem.target_desc: momentum of the crate when the pull stops

givens.desc: mass of the crate
speed of the crate when the pull stops

completion:
SI values: m = 169 kg; v = 318 cm/s = 3.18 m/s.
p = m*v = 169*3.18 = 534.4 kg m/s
In N s: p = 534.4 N s
<steps>
</steps>
<answer>534.4 ± 0 N s</answer>

Determine m, the mass of the crate. Express the result in kg. Report these intermediate quantities in <steps>: v.

During the motion the normal force is N, the kinetic friction force is f_k, the net force is F_net and the acceleration is a1. At the moment the pull is removed, the crate moves with speed v, carries momentum p, and has covered a distance s1. Friction then decelerates it at a rate a2 (magnitude) until it comes to rest after an extra time t2, covering an extra distance s2.

Given:
- It is known that s1 = 5700 mm, where s1 is the distance the crate moves during the pull.
- The time the crate slides after the pull before stopping is t2 = 1220 ms.
- The net horizontal force on the crate during the pull, F_net, equals 31.6 N.
- The mass of the crate, m, equals 22.1 kg.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Determine a2, the magnitude of the crate's deceleration after the pull. Express the result in cm/s^2. In <steps>, report the intermediate values a1, v.
problem.target_desc: magnitude of the crate's deceleration after the pull

givens.desc: net horizontal force on the crate during the pull
mass of the crate
distance the crate moves during the pull
time the crate slides after the pull before stopping

problem.text:
A crate of mass m rests on a level floor, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is mu. Starting from rest, the crate is pulled by a constant horizontal force F for a time t1. While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

Known values:
- h_crate = 62.0 cm (the height of the crate).
- It is known that mu = 0.0756, where mu is the coefficient of kinetic friction.
- s2 = 3360 mm (the distance the crate slides after the pull).
- The distance the crate moves during the pull, s1, equals 2.33 m.
- P_air = 96.4 kPa (the air pressure in the room).
- It is known that F_net = 71.4 N, where F_net is the net horizontal force on the crate during the pull.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Find the mass of the crate, m, in kg. Report these intermediate quantities in <steps>: a2, v, a1.
problem.target_desc: mass of the crate

problem.text:
Starting from rest at a height h, a block of mass m slides down a frictionless ramp; U denotes its potential energy at the top relative to the bottom. At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

Data:
- The natural length of the spring, len_spring, equals 530 mm.
- The mass of the block is m = 343 g.
- It is known that K1 = 3980 mJ, where K1 is the kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Find the speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp, v1, in km/h. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.
problem.target_desc: speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp

givens.desc: kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp
mass of the block

completion:
SI values: K1 = 3980 mJ = 3.98 J; m = 343 g = 0.343 kg.
Not needed: len_spring.
v1 = sqrt(2)*sqrt(K1)/sqrt(m) = sqrt(2)*sqrt(3.98)/sqrt(0.343) = 4.63 m/s
In km/h: v1 = 16.63 km/h
<steps>
</steps>
<answer>16.63 ± 0 km/h</answer>

It then crosses a rough horizontal patch of length L where the coefficient of kinetic friction is mu; friction does work of magnitude W_f on the block, which leaves the patch with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. Finally, on a frictionless floor, the block runs into a light horizontal spring with spring constant k and compresses it by a maximum distance x, at which moment the spring force on the block has magnitude F_s.

Data:
- The speed of the block after the rough patch is v2 = 676 cm/s.
- It is known that K1 = 440 J, where K1 is the kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp.
- It is known that h = 4810 mm, where h is the starting height of the block.
- P_air = 98.9 kPa (the air pressure in the room).
- The natural length of the spring, len_spring, equals 33.2 cm.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

problem.text:
A cart moves along a straight, level track in three phases. In phase 1 it starts with speed u and accelerates uniformly with acceleration a1 for a time t1, covering a distance s1 and reaching speed v. In phase 2 it moves at the constant speed v for a time t2, covering a distance s2. In phase 3 it brakes with a constant deceleration of magnitude b until it comes to rest, which takes a time t3 and covers a distance s3. Over the whole trip the cart covers a total distance d_tot in a total time t_tot, so its average speed is v_avg.

The duration of phase 1, t1, equals 13.9 s. It is known that t3 = 3170 ms, where t3 is the braking time in phase 3. The total duration of the trip is t_tot = 83.7 s.

What is the duration of phase 2, t2? Give your answer in h. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

problem.text:
A crate of mass m rests on a level floor, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is mu. Starting from rest, the crate is pulled by a constant horizontal force F for a time t1. While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

The acceleration of the crate during the pull is a1 = 129 cm/s^2. It is known that v = 237 cm/s, where v is the speed of the crate when the pull stops. It is known that P_air = 99.5 kPa, where P_air is the air pressure in the room. Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Find the distance the crate moves during the pull, s1, in cm. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

problem.text:
Consider a cart on a straight, horizontal track. Phase 1: the cart has initial speed u and speeds up with constant acceleration a1 during a time t1; it travels s1 and ends the phase with speed v. Phase 2: the cart keeps the constant speed v for a time t2 and travels s2. Phase 3: the cart slows down with constant deceleration of magnitude b and stops after a time t3, having travelled s3 in this phase. For the entire motion, d_tot is the total distance, t_tot the total time, and v_avg the average speed.

s3 = 0.115 km (the braking distance in phase 3). The speed of the cart at the end of phase 1 is v = 110 km/h.

Find the braking time in phase 3, t3, in ms. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.
problem.target_desc: braking time in phase 3

givens.desc: braking distance in phase 3
speed of the cart at the end of phase 1

completion:
SI values: s3 = 0.115 km = 115 m; v = 110 km/h = 30.56 m/s.
t3 = 2*s3/v = 2*115/30.56 = 7.354 s
In ms: t3 = 7354 ms
<steps>
</steps>
<answer>7354 ± 1 ms</answer>

- It is known that K2 = 0.0206 kJ, where K2 is the kinetic energy of the block after the rough patch.
- It is known that x = 519 mm, where x is the maximum compression of the spring.

- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

What is the spring constant, k? Give your answer in N/cm. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

maximum compression of the spring

On a horizontal floor sits a crate of mass m; mu is the coefficient of kinetic friction between crate and floor. A constant horizontal pull F acts on the initially resting crate for a time t1. During the motion the normal force is N, the kinetic friction force is f_k, the net force is F_net and the acceleration is a1. At the moment the pull is removed, the crate moves with speed v, carries momentum p, and has covered a distance s1. Friction then decelerates it at a rate a2 (magnitude) until it comes to rest after an extra time t2, covering an extra distance s2.

It is known that F_net = 4090 mN, where F_net is the net horizontal force on the crate during the pull. The duration of the pull is t1 = 2320 ms. The air pressure in the room is P_air = 98.2 kPa. Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Find the momentum of the crate when the pull stops, p, in kg m/s. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

duration of the pull

problem.text:
Starting from rest at a height h, a block of mass m slides down a frictionless ramp; U denotes its potential energy at the top relative to the bottom. At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

It is known that K1 = 52.1 J, where K1 is the kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp. It is known that W_f = 7.11 J, where W_f is the magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch. Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Find the kinetic energy of the block after the rough patch, K2, in J. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.
problem.target_desc: kinetic energy of the block after the rough patch

givens.desc: kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp
magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch

completion:
SI values: K1 = 52.1 J; W_f = 7.11 J.
K2 = K1 - W_f = -7.11 + 52.1 = 44.99 J
<steps>
</steps>
<answer>44.99 ± 0.1 J</answer>

It slides down and reaches the bottom with kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. It then crosses a rough horizontal patch of length L where the coefficient of kinetic friction is mu; friction does work of magnitude W_f on the block, which leaves the patch with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. Finally, on a frictionless floor, the block runs into a light horizontal spring with spring constant k and compresses it by a maximum distance x, at which moment the spring force on the block has magnitude F_s.

The kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp is K1 = 4.15 J. The length of the rough patch is L = 90.3 cm. It is known that h = 238 cm, where h is the starting height of the block. side = 4.27 cm (the side length of the block). It is known that W_f = 0.442 J, where W_f is the magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch. Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Find the coefficient of kinetic friction on the rough patch, mu. Your <steps> must include the intermediate values U, m.
problem.target_desc: coefficient of kinetic friction on the rough patch

Starting from rest at a height h, a block of mass m slides down a frictionless ramp; U denotes its potential energy at the top relative to the bottom. At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

Data:

- It is known that F_s = 112 N, where F_s is the magnitude of the spring force at maximum compression.

- x = 198 mm (the maximum compression of the spring).
- The magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch is W_f = 1.41 J.
- The length of the rough patch is L = 1.42 m.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

problem.text:
Consider a cart on a straight, horizontal track. Phase 1: the cart has initial speed u and speeds up with constant acceleration a1 during a time t1; it travels s1 and ends the phase with speed v. Phase 2: the cart keeps the constant speed v for a time t2 and travels s2. Phase 3: the cart slows down with constant deceleration of magnitude b and stops after a time t3, having travelled s3 in this phase. For the entire motion, d_tot is the total distance, t_tot the total time, and v_avg the average speed.

t3 = 10.7 s (the braking time in phase 3). t1 = 10.5 s (the duration of phase 1). It is known that t_tot = 1.51 min, where t_tot is the total duration of the trip.

Find the duration of phase 2, t2, in s. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.
problem.target_desc: duration of phase 2

givens.desc: duration of phase 1
braking time in phase 3
total duration of the trip

completion:
SI values: t1 = 10.5 s; t3 = 10.7 s; t_tot = 1.51 min = 90.6 s.
t2 = -t1 - t3 + t_tot = -10.5 - 10.7 + 90.6 = 69.4 s
<steps>
</steps>
<answer>69.4 ± 0 s</answer>

In phase 1 it starts with speed u and accelerates uniformly with acceleration a1 for a time t1, covering a distance s1 and reaching speed v. In phase 2 it moves at the constant speed v for a time t2, covering a distance s2. In phase 3 it brakes with a constant deceleration of magnitude b until it comes to rest, which takes a time t3 and covers a distance s3. Over the whole trip the cart covers a total distance d_tot in a total time t_tot, so its average speed is v_avg.

t3 = 0.0513 min (the braking time in phase 3). t1 = 3430 ms (the duration of phase 1). The duration of phase 2, t2, equals 7.11 s.

What is the total duration of the trip, t_tot? Give your answer in s. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

problem.text:
Consider a cart on a straight, horizontal track. Phase 1: the cart has initial speed u and speeds up with constant acceleration a1 during a time t1; it travels s1 and ends the phase with speed v. Phase 2: the cart keeps the constant speed v for a time t2 and travels s2. Phase 3: the cart slows down with constant deceleration of magnitude b and stops after a time t3, having travelled s3 in this phase. For the entire motion, d_tot is the total distance, t_tot the total time, and v_avg the average speed.

The mass of the cart, m_cart, equals 174 kg. The braking time in phase 3 is t3 = 0.0152 min. b = 4.01 m/s^2 (the magnitude of the braking deceleration in phase 3). s2 = 0.278 km (the distance covered during phase 2).

Find the duration of phase 2, t2, in min. In <steps>, report the intermediate values v.

When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

- It is known that s1 = 5340 mm, where s1 is the distance the crate moves during the pull.
- It is known that a1 = 175 cm/s^2, where a1 is the acceleration of the crate during the pull.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

Given:

- It is known that side = 32.2 mm, where side is the side length of the block.
- The coefficient of kinetic friction on the rough patch, mu, equals 0.0759.
- The magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch, W_f, equals 2670 mJ.
- The mass of the block is m = 4.21 kg.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Determine L, the length of the rough patch. Express the result in cm. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

It slides down and reaches the bottom with kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Finally, on a frictionless floor, the block runs into a light horizontal spring with spring constant k and compresses it by a maximum distance x, at which moment the spring force on the block has magnitude F_s.

The gravitational potential energy of the block at the top is U = 2600 mJ. The mass of the block, m, equals 0.375 kg. The natural length of the spring, len_spring, equals 102 mm. Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

problem.text:
A crate of mass m rests on a level floor, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is mu. Starting from rest, the crate is pulled by a constant horizontal force F for a time t1. While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

The net horizontal force on the crate during the pull, F_net, equals 0.427 N. The distance the crate moves during the pull, s1, equals 4.82 m. It is known that a1 = 0.644 m/s^2, where a1 is the acceleration of the crate during the pull. Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

What is the momentum of the crate when the pull stops, p? Give your answer in kg m/s. Report these intermediate quantities in <steps>: t1.

problem.text:
A crate of mass m rests on a level floor, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is mu. Starting from rest, the crate is pulled by a constant horizontal force F for a time t1. While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

The length of the rope used to pull the crate, len_rope, equals 155 cm. The mass of the crate, m, equals 105 kg. It is known that f_k = 101 N, where f_k is the kinetic friction force on the crate. Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Determine a2, the magnitude of the crate's deceleration after the pull. Express the result in cm/s^2. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

Starting from rest, the crate is pulled by a constant horizontal force F for a time t1. While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

Given:
- m = 1.32 kg (the mass of the crate).
- The net horizontal force on the crate during the pull, F_net, equals 2170 mN.
- The momentum of the crate when the pull stops, p, equals 2.74 kg m/s.
- The distance the crate slides after the pull, s2, equals 501 mm.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

What is the magnitude of the applied pulling force, F? Give your answer in mN. In <steps>, report the intermediate values v, a2, f_k.
problem.target_desc: magnitude of the applied pulling force

givens.desc: net horizontal force on the crate during the pull
mass of the crate
momentum of the crate when the pull stops
distance the crate slides after the pull

At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

problem.text:
Consider a cart on a straight, horizontal track. Phase 1: the cart has initial speed u and speeds up with constant acceleration a1 during a time t1; it travels s1 and ends the phase with speed v. Phase 2: the cart keeps the constant speed v for a time t2 and travels s2. Phase 3: the cart slows down with constant deceleration of magnitude b and stops after a time t3, having travelled s3 in this phase. For the entire motion, d_tot is the total distance, t_tot the total time, and v_avg the average speed.

Data:
- a1 = 1.35 m/s^2 (the acceleration of the cart during phase 1).
- The distance covered during phase 1 is s1 = 0.0486 km.
- The mass of the cart, m_cart, equals 384 kg.
- The speed of the cart at the end of phase 1 is v = 1530 cm/s.
- The length of the cart is len_cart = 1.63 m.

Find the speed of the cart at the start of phase 1, u, in m/s. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.
problem.target_desc: speed of the cart at the start of phase 1

givens.desc: acceleration of the cart during phase 1
distance covered during phase 1
speed of the cart at the end of phase 1

completion:
SI values: a1 = 1.35 m/s^2; s1 = 0.0486 km = 48.6 m; v = 1530 cm/s = 15.3 m/s.
Not needed: len_cart, m_cart.
u = sqrt(-2*a1*s1 + v**2) = sqrt(-2*1.35*48.6 + 15.3**2) = 9.533 m/s
<steps>
</steps>
<answer>9.533 ± 0.01 m/s</answer>

problem.text:
A cart moves along a straight, level track in three phases. In phase 1 it starts with speed u and accelerates uniformly with acceleration a1 for a time t1, covering a distance s1 and reaching speed v. In phase 2 it moves at the constant speed v for a time t2, covering a distance s2. In phase 3 it brakes with a constant deceleration of magnitude b until it comes to rest, which takes a time t3 and covers a distance s3. Over the whole trip the cart covers a total distance d_tot in a total time t_tot, so its average speed is v_avg.

Data:
- The average speed of the cart over the whole trip, v_avg, equals 27.9 km/h.
- The total distance covered by the cart, d_tot, equals 385 m.
- It is known that w_track = 1.99 m, where w_track is the width of the track.
- The mass of the cart is m_cart = 96.9 kg.

What is the total duration of the trip, t_tot? Give your answer in min. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

Known values:
- L = 6.11 m (the length of the rough patch).
- The speed of the block after the rough patch is v2 = 620 cm/s.
- The coefficient of kinetic friction on the rough patch, mu, equals 0.172.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Find the speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp, v1, in m/s. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.
problem.target_desc: speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp

givens.desc: length of the rough patch

problem.text:
A block of mass m is released from rest at height h on a frictionless ramp. At the top, its gravitational potential energy relative to the bottom of the ramp is U. It slides down and reaches the bottom with kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. It then crosses a rough horizontal patch of length L where the coefficient of kinetic friction is mu; friction does work of magnitude W_f on the block, which leaves the patch with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. Finally, on a frictionless floor, the block runs into a light horizontal spring with spring constant k and compresses it by a maximum distance x, at which moment the spring force on the block has magnitude F_s.

Data:
- The kinetic energy of the block after the rough patch, K2, equals 0.111 kJ.
- The spring constant, k, equals 66.9 kN/m.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Determine F_s, the magnitude of the spring force at maximum compression. Express the result in kN. Your <steps> must include the intermediate values x.
problem.target_desc: magnitude of the spring force at maximum compression

givens.desc: kinetic energy of the block after the rough patch
spring constant

completion:
SI values: K2 = 0.111 kJ = 111 J; k = 66.9 kN/m = 6.69e+04 N/m.
x = sqrt(2)*sqrt(K2)/sqrt(k) = sqrt(2)*sqrt(111)/sqrt(6.69e+04) = 0.1425 m
F_s = k*x = 0.1425*6.69e+04 = 9559 N
In kN: F_s = 9.559 kN
<steps>
x = 0.1425 m
</steps>
<answer>9.559 ± 0.001 kN</answer>

It then crosses a rough horizontal patch of length L where the coefficient of kinetic friction is mu; friction does work of magnitude W_f on the block, which leaves the patch with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. Finally, on a frictionless floor, the block runs into a light horizontal spring with spring constant k and compresses it by a maximum distance x, at which moment the spring force on the block has magnitude F_s.

- len_spring = 0.114 m (the natural length of the spring).
- v1 = 1910 cm/s (the speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp).
- It is known that m = 191 g, where m is the mass of the block.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

problem.text:
A cart moves along a straight, level track in three phases. In phase 1 it starts with speed u and accelerates uniformly with acceleration a1 for a time t1, covering a distance s1 and reaching speed v. In phase 2 it moves at the constant speed v for a time t2, covering a distance s2. In phase 3 it brakes with a constant deceleration of magnitude b until it comes to rest, which takes a time t3 and covers a distance s3. Over the whole trip the cart covers a total distance d_tot in a total time t_tot, so its average speed is v_avg.

It is known that v = 16.9 m/s, where v is the speed of the cart at the end of phase 1. The speed of the cart at the start of phase 1, u, equals 1.90 km/h. The acceleration of the cart during phase 1 is a1 = 171 cm/s^2.

What is the duration of phase 1, t1? Give your answer in ms. Show your calculation first; no intermediate values need to be listed in <steps>.

While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

It slides down and reaches the bottom with kinetic energy K1 and speed v1.
